findings.passage:
Securing elections from each citizen’s registration to the final count of legal votes by:
Requiring proof of citizenship to register to vote.
Requiring the Counties and the Secretary of State to update the voter rolls at least quarterly.
Requiring a mandatory photo ID for every election, without exception.
Restricting mail-in ballots to disabled, military, and eligible citizens who are out of their county for the entire voting period.
findings.note: Campaign issues page, under a 'Secure Texas Elections' heading in a priorities list. The page is undated; it was read on 2026-10-28 and carries 2026 campaign content. It backs proof of citizenship to register, quarterly voter-roll updates, photo ID at every election with no exceptions, and mail ballots only for disabled, military and out-of-county voters.

findings.passage: Codifies in the Texas Constitution that only U.S. citizens can vote in Texas elections, emphasizing current laws.
findings.note: Her written summary of Prop 16 on the November 4, 2025 ballot (ballot wording: a voter must be a United States citizen). Her listed recommendation on that page is FOR. Page is undated; month taken from the election it describes.

findings.passage: We had wins in Election Integrity like SB 2753 by Sen. Bob Hall which standardized in-person voting with no gap between early voting and Election Day
findings.note: Her 2025 session summary lists SB 2753 (in-person voting schedule) as an election integrity win. It is about voting schedules, not ID. Page is undated; year taken from the 2025 session it reports.
